title: Coherent sheaves with free stalks are locally free
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent [pqf-def-coherent] $\mathcal O_X$-module. If every stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is a finite free $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module, then $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0GWM (algebra-lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free), applied on affine opens where a coherent module on a locally Noetherian scheme is finitely presented; as used in the proof of Divisors Tag 0CC4 (with Algebra Tag 00NX)

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], since $X$ is locally Noetherian, $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. By [pqf-def-locnoeth], $X$ has an affine open covering $X=\bigcup_iU_i$ with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ and $A_i$ Noetherian. Fix one such $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c), $M=\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$ is a finite $A$-module, and by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3), applied to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F|_U$, the counit $\widetilde M\to\mathcal F|_U$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, coherent modules on locally Noetherian schemes

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ with point $x\in U$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] gives $\mathcal F_x\cong\widetilde M_x\cong M_{\mathfrak p}$ as modules over $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$, so $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finite free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module by hypothesis. The affine criterion [lem-sc-affine-finite-module-free-locus] then gives $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$ generating the unit ideal with each $M_{f_i}$ finite free over $A_{f_i}$; equivalently $\widetilde M\cong\mathcal F|_U$ is finite locally free on $U$.

The $U_i$ of Step 1 cover $X$; collecting, over all $i$, the open covers of $U_i$ on which $\mathcal F$ is finite free given by Step 2 yields an open cover of $X$ on which $\mathcal F$ is finite free. This is precisely the definition of a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module.
